qAndA.answer: The flashlight can use either three AAA batteries with the included adapter or a single 18650 battery.
qAndA.question: What types of batteries can the flashlight use?

qAndA.answer: The beam can be focused by extending the head of the flashlight outwards or spread by retracting it inwards.
qAndA.question: How do you adjust the beam of the flashlight?

qAndA.answer: The scalloped edge can be used for self-defense by striking an attacker and leaving a distinctive mark for identification.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the scalloped edge on the flashlight's bezel?

qAndA.answer: The beam has a square shape due to the type of LED used in the flashlight.
qAndA.question: What is unique about the shape of the flashlight's beam?

qAndA.answer: The strobe mode can be used to disorient an attacker, create a distraction, or signal for help.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the strobe mode on the flashlight?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello everybody, welcome back to the world of me. My name is Cougar and this is another episode from our camping and survival series.
We've got a new box in today and go ahead and get it opened up. Now this is, as you can see here, the XT808 tactical flashlight.
And it is by primitive survivors. You know, this one actually kind of stood out as, you know, the features that it has.
Now as you can see here, it is a very small one. It is only about six inches long roughly. It does have this simple little lanyard here.
It is turned on and off by the simple push button on the back.
Now if you look at the side here, you can see there's some numbers and everything right there.
And those actually represent one of the features, which is what it does is this.
As you can see, it extends out and goes, you know, basically it just goes in and out.
By doing that, you're actually changing the beam.
So like some lights, for example, a mag light where you sit there and turn the end and it will increase or decrease the diameter of the beam.
This does the same thing where you can bring it out and that will focus the beam down or you can bring it back and it will spread the beam out.
Now something else, this is pretty cool in the aspect that this does actually take two different types of battery.
You can use, as it shows here, with the little adapter, three triple A batteries that can go inside here.
Or you can take and use, for example, this sleeve and use one of these right here.
Now this basically looks like a really big double A battery.
But what it actually is, this is an 1865 battery.
These, of course, are a much higher powered type of battery.
You just take and slide it into the sleeve here and go according, just like this one does where you have the little button end on the end there.
You have the button end here.
You slide it in that way, like that.
And then it has the little piece at the back end to contact the flat and tighten this up.
And here we go.
And of course, as you can see, that does darken it up quite a lot.
You can see the area that this is focusing on here. It's very, very bright.
And as we go, we'll open it out and then as I draw it down, you can see I'm focusing it out.
And you can see that's actually a square.
And that square is because of the type of LED that it has.
Another feature that it has is that it actually has different stages.
The first one, this is, of course, high.
And it's, of course, very hard to tell with the camera because, of course, the camera dims down and everything like that.
And then this is low. And you can see I'm even brighter here.
So at low, this is still a pretty bright flashlight.
This is brighter, definitely, than the standard 2D flashlights that you get at the local hardware store.
And then you have the strobe effect. And of course, that one is a good one for if necessary.
You can use it in the case of, if there's an attacker, you could flip it over real quick and flash them.
And kind of temporarily blind them so you can get away.
As well as it's, of course, an attention grabber when you're looking at it from far distances.
And then, if we go to this last one, like I showed you before,
this is actually the help signal. This is the SOS pattern.
Now, this isn't super heavy. It is a machined aircraft aluminum.
As I understand, it does have this little tip on the end.
It has kind of the scalloped edge to it.
And if I remember correctly, the scalloped edge a lot of times is for marking.
